title: ERASE_Evaluation of early treatment response of soft tissue sarcomas under neoadjuvant hyperthermia and chemotherapy using functional MRI as well as FDG PET-CT
summary:
Soft tissue sarcomas are rare malignancies that require very prompt and aggressive treatment after initial diagnosis. Treatment regimens are based on clinical, histologic, and imaging presentation of the tumor in addition to patient preference. Imaging techniques are used to evaluate treatment response in order to monitor the success of neoadjuvant therapy. 
What is the predictive value of DCE-MRI and MR diffusion imaging on tumor-free and progression-free survival under neoadjuvant combined chemotherapy and hyperthermia and further, to what extent do these methods provide concordant, complementary or contrasting information to PET-CT.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bone and articular cartilage of other and unspecified sites

interventions.name: Patients will be selected according to the inclusion criteria after examination at the LMU Clinic and Polyclinic, informed about the procedure at least 24h before the examination. Imaging such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and positron emission tomography (PET-CT) examination are performed for

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Soft tissue sarcoma of the extremities in tumor stage AJCC III with indication for neoadjuvant combined chemotherapy/hyperthermia 
- Tumor board decision for treatment chemotherapy/hyperthermia
- Indication for MRI and PET-CT examinations as part of clinical care for soft tissue sarcoma 
- > 18 years male/female
- GFR value >30ml/min 
- Signed declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Contraindications to MRI examination, especially implants not suitable for MR, tattoos or piercings, pronounced claustrophobia
- Lack of consent and/or lack of ability to consent to the study 
- Pregnancy
- Known allergy to MR contrast agent or PET-CT tracer
- GFR < 30 ml/min with renal insufficiency
